original.target_description: Experiment 2 behavioral inferences, rank-judgment accuracy, cue regressions, and mediation are multiple candidates; supplied locator/description does not uniquely identify a test.

notes: Target correspondence unresolved. Both rows specify Experiment 2; neither identifies an outcome, predictor, contrast, or model. Locator p. 7/p. 8 does not select one test. Proof printed pp. 1–12 differ from cited final issue pp. 3–14; both relevant printed pages were inspected. No mapping inferred from row order, numeric values, or PDF highlighting. Candidate tests on printed p. 7 (PDF p. 8): condition main effect on hierarchy-based behavioral inferences F(1,55)=83.67,p<.001; overall rank-judgment accuracy F(1,28)=91.39,p<.001; speaker-sex effect on accuracy F(1,28)=5.90,p<.05; pitch cue F(1,50)=5.70,p<.05. Table 6 prints six cue slopes and eta-squared values. Printed p. 8 (PDF p. 9): loudness F(1,50)=20.54,p<.001; loudness variability F(1,50)=8.09,p<.01; condition/inference path b=0.77 with F(1,55)=83.67,p<.001 before adjustment and b=0.46 with F(1,25)=2.19,p>.16 after adjustment. Fig. 2 prints multiple standardized partial-regression coefficients, while analysis text describes unstandardized regression coefficients. These are unassigned candidates only. Sample roles: printed p. 6 describes 40 recruited perceivers and a voice subset of 30 female and 30 male speakers. Candidate voice subset arithmetic: 30 + 30 = 60 speakers, with mutually exclusive speaker-sex groups; no row-specific final analytic model N established. Printed p. 11 Note 1 reports 11 perceivers unusable because judgments had no variance. This is a distinct perceiver role, not an exclusion from the voice subset. No N inferred from df or final perceiver N calculated. Speaker-selection criteria and additional analyses are referenced in an unsupplied supplement. Rendered PDF pp. 8–9 inspected for layout; quotes are ordered canonical text fragments. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders. Requested d is not printed for these candidate tests: alternatives include eta-squared, slopes, F statistics, and regression coefficients. No conversion performed.
